name: High Oak
ecological_role: major canopy tree; mast producer; habitat support
cultural_role: structural wood for sanctioned deadfall harvest
description: The Feywood's dominant oak lineage, basin-analog grown to older, broader proportions under the Glade's conditions. Long-lived and habitat-rich; its mast supports silverbough hart, gladehorn stag, and the canopy squirrel population across the outer wild.

name: Elderoak
ecological_role: climax canopy dominant; Heartwood-conditioned variant of High Oak
cultural_role: structural and symbolic; oldest Thornveil groves
description: A Feywood-amplified lineage of High Oak produced under sustained Heartwood influence. Elderoaks dominate Thornveil's older groves and the Outer Wild's climax stands. Their scale and age-span exceed any realm-side oak; individuals carry house-records in their growth that trained elven readers parse as living archive.

name: Grey Beech
ecological_role: shade canopy; fungal network host
cultural_role: fine wood for quiet interior construction
description: A major shade-tolerant canopy species, widespread across the mature Glade. Grey Beech hosts substantial Rootlace Mycelium connection and provides the wood most favored for finishing work in interior living spaces.

name: Silverbeech
ecological_role: Feywood-conditioned beech; shade-favoring climax associate
cultural_role: associated with mature Glade interiors; ceremonial connotations
description: A pale-barked beech lineage shaped by sustained Heartwood-field exposure. Silverbeech favors shaded mature interiors and the margins of the Silent Grove. Its pale wood carries a distinctive ambient-field resonance that trained elves can feel.

name: Silverbark Ash
ecological_role: mid-canopy; edge stabilizer; flexible growth
cultural_role: spear shafts, training weapons, light frameworks
description: A resilient ash lineage straighter and more flexible than realm-side ash. Silverbark Ash is the canonical elven wood for spear shafts, training weapons, and light frameworks. Harvested from sanctioned deadfall and occasional selective cut.

name: Ironroot Hardwood
ecological_role: dense slow-growing canopy species
cultural_role: load-bearing wood, shield cores, long-service tools
description: A dense hardwood of the deep wild, harvested only from natural fall or sanctioned selective cut. Ironroot is the structural wood of choice for shield cores, load-bearing construction, and tools expected to last across generations.

name: Longbough
ecological_role: uncommon canopy species; exceptionally long-lived individuals
cultural_role: canonical elven longbow wood; harvested only from offered limbs or natural fall
description: The canonical wood of elven longbows. Longbough is never cut from living standing timber; material comes only from trees that naturally fall or that offer themselves through druidic sign. Sylvara's longbow is Longbough. The Heartwood bow carried by Lethariel is Longbough crafted from a limb offered in connection with the Heartwood branch sign before the Discordant War.

name: Witheroak
ecological_role: rare variant appearing under sustained Glade strain
cultural_role: ritual marking; health-register indicator; specific ceremonial use
description: A rare variant of High Oak that appears when the Glade is under sustained strain — dark-grained, dense, ritually significant. Its presence itself is a health-register indicator. Druids mark witheroak when it appears; living witheroak wood is never exported and is used only for specific ceremonial purposes during Glade strain.

name: Resinheart Pine
ecological_role: edge and upland conifer
cultural_role: resin, sealant, incense, waterproofing
description: An edge and upland conifer, more common where the ambient field is thinner and light stronger. Resinheart Pine produces the resin used across the Glade for sealant, incense, and waterproofing applications; it is a significant export category.

name: The Heartwood
ecological_role: living center and ambient-field anchor of the Glade
cultural_role: sacred center of elven civilization
description: A singular ancient tree of deciduous form, girth beyond a dozen adults' linked reach. Species indeterminate — not identified with any realm tree lineage. The Heartwood is the living center of the Feywood Glade and the anchor of its ambient relational field. The Glade is the Heartwood and the Heartwood is the Glade. Never harvested in any form.

name: The Elder Trees of the Silent Grove
ecological_role: foundational substrate of the Glade's root-memory network
cultural_role: sacred; older than any other old-growth; never harvested
description: Several dozen individuals of indeterminate species, older than any other old-growth in the Glade. The Elder Trees predate the Heartwood's central role and form the foundational substrate of the Glade's root-memory network. Never harvested.

name: Thornveil Vine
ecological_role: climbing thorn-vine; pollinator support; cover and barrier
cultural_role: Thornveil's name-origin; protective planting around sacred sites
description: The climbing thorn-vine that gives Thornveil its name — historically the living thorn-veil maintained around the Heartwood in the city's founding era. Used today as protective planting around select sacred boundaries and managed civic plantings.

name: Oathvine
ecological_role: flowering climbing vine; pollinator support
cultural_role: ceremonial; paired with Oathbloom; records family oaths across generations
description: A ceremonial flowering climber used in house rites, oath observances, memorial plantings, and funeral rites. Oathvine and Oathbloom are the paired ceremonial flora marking elven oath-life. House Heartwood maintains Oathvine at the Estate and at the Thornveil seat; each family's oath-plot carries Oathvine growth patterns that read as the living record of the house's vows across generations.

name: Veilvine
ecological_role: climbing vine with distinctive seasonal color shift
cultural_role: early-warning Turning indicator monitored by druids
description: A climbing vine whose distinctive seasonal color shift precedes broader canopy color change. Druids monitor Veilvine as an early-warning indicator of Turning onset; its color transition registers days to weeks before the larger forest follows.

name: Thornfiber Cane
ecological_role: fast-growing flexible cane-vine
cultural_role: basketry, binding, training apparatus, light framework
description: A fast-growing flexible cane-vine gathered from the Heartwater Basin margins and the Glade Edge. Thornfiber is the canonical elven fiber for basketry, binding, training apparatus, and light framework construction. A significant trade export in refined forms.

name: Sweetbriar
ecological_role: flowering climber; pollinator support
cultural_role: domestic ornamental; common around Thornveil residences
description: A flowering climber with faintly sweet scent, common around Thornveil residences. Sweetbriar is the Glade's domestic ornamental climber, widely planted in family gardens and cluster common spaces.

name: Hearthnut Grove Tree
ecological_role: major nut producer; canopy squirrel and songbird forage
cultural_role: winter food-security staple; flour, meal, oil
description: The quiet backbone food species of the Glade. Hearthnut produces the nuts, oil, meal, and flour-equivalent that sustain elven subsistence through winter. Hearthnut groves are tended at Thornveil, Vaelmere, noble estates, and the Glade Edge; the species is central to elven food culture in a way realm observers often underestimate.

name: Summerpear Bough
ecological_role: cultivated soft-fruit tree
cultural_role: fresh fruit, preserves, dried stores, wine base
description: A cultivated soft-fruit tree providing fresh fruit, preserves, dried stores, and wine base across the Glade. Summerpear orchards are a standard feature of elven estates and cluster gardens.

name: Goldcap Apple
ecological_role: hardy long-keeping cultivated fruit
cultural_role: cider, vinegar, preserves, trade export
description: A hardy long-keeping cultivated fruit grown at Vaelmere, Thornveil's outer groves, and noble estates. Goldcap is the canonical source of Goldcap cider — a core forest-wine tradition — and also produces vinegar and preserves. Among the Feywood's most recognized trade exports.

name: Dewberry Bramble
ecological_role: edge berry shrub; major forage for birds, foxes, bears, gatherers
cultural_role: wine base; preserves
description: An edge berry shrub providing major forage for birds, duskpetal fox, oldroot bear, and elven gatherers. Dewberry is a canonical forest-wine base and a common preserve ingredient.

name: Antlerthorn
ecological_role: thorned browse shrub; major cervid forage and cover
cultural_role: boundary hedge and hunt-lore marker in the outer wild
description: A thorned browse shrub common in the outer wild and lighter glade-edge margins. Antlerthorn is one of the defining forage plants for silverbough hart and gladehorn stag, and its dense growth creates cover corridors along old game paths. Elven hunters read antlerthorn damage patterns as a sign of herd movement and seasonal pressure.

name: Shadefern Root
ecological_role: edible root in low-light systems
cultural_role: soups, mash, travel food, household starch source
description: An edible root native to the Glade's low-light understory. Shadefern is cultivated in Thornveil's shaded understory plots and noble compounds; it serves as the Glade's primary starch source for soups, mash, and travel food.

name: River Reed Onion
ecological_role: riparian culinary plant
cultural_role: standard elven riparian cultivation; household kitchen staple
description: A riparian culinary plant cultivated along the Heartwater Basin margins, streamside plots, and estate water margins. River Reed Onion is a Glade kitchen staple; its riparian cultivation is one of the Basin's continuous human-use activities.

name: Hearthlight Fungus
ecological_role: canonical bioluminescent understory species
cultural_role: primary visible health-register indicator; ambient illumination
description: The Glade's canonical bioluminescent understory fungus, visible even in daylight at the Border. Hearthlight brightness correlates with ambient-field strength and serves as the primary visible indicator of Glade health. Its dimming is one of the earliest visible Turning signals; its steady glow under Standing Green provides ambient illumination under heavy canopy.

name: Rootlace Mycelium
ecological_role: foundational fungal network; nutrient exchange; root-memory substrate
cultural_role: substrate through which the Heartwood's root-memory operates
description: The foundational fungal network underlying all Feywood soils. Rootlace handles nutrient distribution between canopy trees and understory plants, carries decomposition-chain continuity, and serves as the biological substrate through which the Heartwood's root-memory network extends beyond its physical roots. Druids read Rootlace disturbance patterns to monitor Glade-wide stress from localized observation.

name: Heartmorel
ecological_role: edible decomposer fungus
cultural_role: signature Glade culinary fungus; Vaelmere trade export
description: An edible decomposer fungus seasonal to the Glade's mature forest. Heartmorel is the canonical Glade culinary fungus; preserved Heartmorel is a minor but recognized Vaelmere trade export.

name: Redveil Shelf
ecological_role: medicinal shelf fungus on fallen timber
cultural_role: fever remedies, wound preparations
description: A medicinal shelf fungus harvested from fallen timber. Redveil preparations are used in fever remedies and wound preparations across the Glade's medicinal tradition.

name: Grove Deepmoss
ecological_role: signature ground cover of the Silent Grove
cultural_role: slow-change sign of deeper instability; druidic-use-only
description: The signature ground cover of the Silent Grove Enclave. Grove Deepmoss changes slowly, and its shift is among the last indicators to register in the Glade's seven-stage decline order — any visible change in Grove Deepmoss signals deep instability. Druidic use only, in tiny amounts if at all.

name: Winterglass Lichen
ecological_role: bark and stone lichen; moisture and air-quality indicator
cultural_role: dye, ritual marking ink, fine medicinal preparations
description: A slow-growing bark and stone lichen of the Silent Grove, sacred stones, and cool shaded margins. Winterglass is a moisture and air-quality indicator, and its careful harvest yields dyes, ritual-marking ink, and fine medicinal preparations.

name: Heartbloom
ecological_role: rare pollinator flower of the Heartwood understory
cultural_role: sacred observance; never casually harvested
description: A rare pollinator flower of the Heartwood's understory, found only or almost only within the Heartwood Core. Heartbloom is an object of sacred observance; it is never casually harvested.

name: Dawngold Bloom
ecological_role: ceremonial flower tied to the Heartwood's Dawn-Gold light quality
cultural_role: sacred observance; paired with Eveningjade in Heartwood light-cycle reinforcement
description: A ceremonial flower tied to the Heartwood's canonical Dawn-Gold light quality. Dawngold grows at the Heartwood's margins and in select sacred plantings. Paired with Eveningjade as reinforcement of the named light cycles; used in observance and symbolic language.

name: Eveningjade Bloom
ecological_role: ceremonial flower tied to the Heartwood's Evening-Jade light quality
cultural_role: sacred observance; paired with Dawngold in Heartwood light-cycle reinforcement
description: A ceremonial flower tied to the Heartwood's canonical Evening-Jade light quality. Eveningjade grows alongside Dawngold at the Heartwood's margins and in select sacred plantings; the two together reinforce the named light cycles in ceremonial and symbolic practice.

name: Oathbloom
ecological_role: ceremonial flower; paired with Oathvine
cultural_role: canonical source of oath-marking ceremonial infusion; never exported
description: A ceremonial flower paired with Oathvine, cultivated at Heartwood observance margins, noble family sacred plots, and Grove-adjacent ritual spaces. Oathbloom is the canonical source of ceremonial infusion used in oath-marking events — Heartwarden oaths, marriage oaths, house oaths, induction observances. The infusion is not a trade good; it is made and consumed in the context of the oath itself. A shared Oathbloom draught is the ceremony embodied. Tended by the druid order and by the houses at their own oath-plots.

name: Silverleaf Balm
ecological_role: medicinal herb; pollinator support
cultural_role: healer's staple; salves, wound wash, calming infusions; trade export
description: A foundational medicinal herb of Feywood medicine. Silverleaf preparations yield salves, wound wash, and calming infusions; the herb is cultivated in Thornveil's tended plots and across noble estates. Refined preparations are a recognized Vaelmere trade export.

name: Dawnmint
ecological_role: aromatic culinary herb
cultural_role: tea, scenting, cooking, household medicine
description: An aromatic culinary herb with mild medicinal properties, cultivated widely across the Glade's domestic gardens. Dawnmint supports tea, scenting, cooking, and household medicine; its preparations are a minor trade export.

name: Amberbell Flower
ecological_role: bell-flower pollinator species; seasonal bloom marker
cultural_role: common wine flavoring
description: A bell-flower species supporting Honeybound bees and other pollinators. Amberbell is a seasonal bloom marker and a common flavoring in Feywood wines; its appearance through the warm season is one of the Glade's visible thresholds.
